name: Jelly Sauce No. 2
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: lemon—juice and half the grated peel
ingredients.originalText: 1 lemon—juice and half the grated peel

ingredients.name: glasses wine, and a tablespoonful powdered sugar
ingredients.originalText: 2 glasses wine, and a tablespoonful powdered sugar

instructions.text: Heat the butter a little more than blood-warm; beat the jelly to a smooth batter and add gradually the butter, the lemon, and nutmeg.
Warm almost to a boil, stirring all the while; beat hard, put in the sugar, lastly the wine.
Set in a vessel of hot water stirring now and then, until it is wanted.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat the butter a little more than blood-warm; beat the jelly to a smooth batter and add gradually the butter, the lemon, and nutmeg.
2. Warm almost to a boil, stirring all the while; beat hard, put in the sugar, lastly the wine.
3. Set in a vessel of hot water stirring now and then, until it is wanted.
4. Keep it covered to hinder the escape of the wine flavor.
5. Stir well before pouring out.
